title: feat: let an approved app submission close and pay a quest
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Addresses #15527

- Adds an optional **Quest** field to the app submission form (`#123` or `123`); its description tells everyone else to leave it empty
- Validation (at review and at approval) requires an open POLLEN-QUEST issue; otherwise the submission moves to `APP-NEEDS-INFO`
- The catalog PR says `Fixes #<submission>, fixes #<quest>`
- The quest check pays the commit co-author of PRs by the `pollinations-ai[bot]` app (a Bot, not the same-named user) on `auto/app-<n>-` branches; other PRs still pay only their author
- CONTRIBUTING, the Pollen FAQ, the social brand prompt and AGENTS.md explain app quests

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Quest closed by an approved app | Closes, pays nobody (bot author) | Pays the submitter |
| Quest search cost | 3 points | 3 points + 1 per catalog PR closing a quest |

Tests: enter `test/quests.test.ts` 41/41 (new test fails on old code); `submission.test.js` 7/7. Both GraphQL queries checked against live GitHub.

Needs an enter production deploy before the first such quest pays.

gist.headline: Apps can finish quests now
gist.blurb: Built an app for a Quest? Put its number on the submission form. Once the app is approved, the Quest closes and its Pollen reward goes to the submitter—not the publishing bot.
gist.summary: App submissions now accept an optional Quest number (#123 or 123), validate that it points to an open POLLEN-QUEST issue, and close the Quest on approval while attributing the reward to the submitter.
gist.impact: App builders can submit an app for an open Quest and claim its Pollen reward after approval, even though the catalog PR is opened by pollinations-ai[bot].
gist.visual_concept: An app submission card marked with a Quest number becomes a blooming flower in the app catalog; a small Pollen token reaches Polli rather than the friendly publishing robot. Show Polli placing the card and the robot helping tend the catalog garden.
